decision: Accept CVE-2019-1010022 and CVE-2019-1010024 as low practical risks for the reviewed reference installation.

instructions: If they are not really a thread and are listed as low risk issues then we can ignore them, this also apply for all CVEs we encounter.
Of course, if there are available listed fixes then we can apply fixes

policy_scope: Risk-based assessment applies to all CVEs; apply available compatible vendor fixes as the default. Findings assessed as low practical risk may be documented as accepted; scanner severity alone does not decide applicability or risk.
supersedes: Earlier requirement for an applied fix or complete supported-caller exclusion for every finding, including all low-risk findings.

reasons.CVE-2019-1010022: Accepted low practical risk: a stack-guard mitigation bypass requiring a separate native stack-buffer overflow. No independent RateFreak attack was demonstrated. Debian marks it unimportant and Ubuntu assigns low priority; the native protection weakness remains present.
reasons.CVE-2019-1010024: Accepted low practical risk: predictable native stack addresses may assist exploitation of a separate memory-corruption flaw. No independent RateFreak attack was demonstrated. Debian marks it unimportant; tested address reuse remains present even with the stack cache disabled.

fix_status.vendor_package_fix: No fixed Debian version listed for either ID in the reviewed primary sources.
fix_status.upstream_candidate: A TLS guard-page RFC exists for 1010022; it is not an applied or qualified vendor fix.
fix_status.future_action: Apply and validate available compatible vendor fixes; revisit these acceptances when fixes or risk evidence change.

technical_limits: The stack-guard/address-reuse behavior remains present; no remediation or complete caller exclusion is claimed.
Separate native memory-corruption flaws could make these weaknesses relevant. This acceptance does not cover newly discovered exploits or changed exposure.
API Ubuntu libc behavior was also observed in the earlier probe; this decision covers the reviewed reference installation, though the previous six scanner records concern web/tools/PostgreSQL.
Previous native, decoder, JIT, allocator and supported-caller conditions remain in force.
This is a policy/disposition change. No runtime change, new application test run, refreshed scan, stable qualification or publication is claimed.
remaining_release_work: Final reference acceptance, representative capacity and security-report notification delivery
